speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I’m Dr. Agent. Can you describe the nature of your headache and specify if the vision loss is in one eye or both?

speaker: Patient
text: 69-year-old woman. The patient reports a 3-week history of headache and progressively worsening vision. She has not noticed any other symptoms, including no recent weight changes, no fevers, no night sweats, and no pain elsewhere in the body.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience any jaw pain when chewing or scalp tenderness, and have you noticed any swelling or tenderness in the temples?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Headache. I also have Worsening vision over the past 3 weeks, No weight changes, No fevers, No night sweats, No other pain.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: ESR, CRP
Do you have any history of hypertension, diabetes, or prior eye surgery, and have you noticed any double vision or difficulty looking in certain directions?

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal inflammatory markers, we need to rule out structural causes like a tumor or aneurysm. REQUEST TEST: MRI Brain with contrast

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Fundoscopy, Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT)
Since systemic inflammation and brain MRI are normal, I need to examine the optic nerve and retina directly to assess for ischemic or compressive optic neuropathy.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Fundoscopy shows findings suggestive of retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages. Visual Acuity is 20/120 in the Right Eye and 20/80 in the Left Eye.

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal inflammatory markers and brain MRI effectively rule out giant cell arteritis and intracranial masses. Since the fundoscopy reveals retinal vein occlusion or hemorrhages, this points toward a vascular or coagulopathic etiology rather than an inflammatory one. I need to assess your cardiovascular risk factors; do you have a history of hypertension, hyperlipidemia, or atrial fibrillation?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: The patient has hypertension, which is controlled with medication. She also has a history of high cholesterol. Social history: Retired school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially. No recreational drug use.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the bilateral retinal findings and controlled hypertension, I suspect a coagulopathy or hematologic malignancy. REQUEST TEST: CBC, Peripheral Smear, Viscosity

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Hemoglobin: 14.2 g/dL. Peripheral Blood Smear: Findings indicative of increased circulating immunoglobulins. Serum Electrophoresis: Increased concentration of a pentameric immunoglobulin, consistent with a monoclonal gammopathy.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of pentameric immunoglobulins (IgM) and increased viscosity strongly suggests Waldenström Macroglobulinemia causing hyperviscosity syndrome. DIAGNOSIS READY: Waldenström Macroglobulinemia
